summary.headline: Godavari Biorefineries FY26 total income rose 6% to INR2,000 crore and EBITDA 15.8% to INR139 crore, with Q4 EBITDA of INR92 crore (16.2% margin).
summary.overview: FY26 total income was INR2,000.2 crore (up 6% from INR1,886.9 crore) and EBITDA was INR139.3 crore (up 15.8% from INR120.3 crore), with full-year margin around 7%. Profit after tax was INR3.5 crore versus a loss in FY25. Q4 revenue from operations was INR564 crore, EBITDA INR92 crore (margin 16.2% versus 9.8% in Q3), and PAT INR52.9 crore versus INR8.3 crore in Q3, driven by a record 2.5 million tonne crushing season. Management said the bio-based chemicals outlook is stronger from Q1 FY27, helped by higher import costs and narrowing fossil-to-bio price gaps, while the 200 KLPD grain distillery is nearing commissioning trials.

segments.name: Integrated sugar, ethanol and co-generation
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR1,383 crore and EBITDA INR97.4 crore (up 19% YoY). Q4 revenue about INR411 crore, with margin gains from higher crushing volumes and better recoveries; highest-ever cane crushing of 2.5 million tonnes.

segments.name: Bio-based chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 segment revenue INR578 crore; Q4 revenue about INR147 crore. Specialty chemicals rose to 61% of segment revenue from 58% YoY, though geopolitical disruption hit sales and the call did not give segment EBITDA.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR658 crore on improved B-heavy molasses availability; about 98 million litres sold (ethanol blending programme, ENA and other grades). About 81% of volume went to EBP per analyst question, which management did not dispute.

segments.name: Jivana (consumer business)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR129 crore; management cites growing retail presence across South India, with no margin or growth rate disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects stronger bio-based chemicals performance from Q1 FY27, with debottlenecking benefits from FY25 showing through in FY27.

200 KLPD grain-based distillery (about 60 million litres a year) to start commissioning trials in June 2026, with some business in Q2 FY27; larger benefits expected from the ethanol year starting November.
Government ethanol pricing and EBP targets expected around September or October 2026; management will then give clearer economics for the new capacity.
Management said the company may use surplus ethanol for its own ethyl acetate and chemicals production, given higher imported ethanol costs.
DME (CO2 and hydrogen) pilot plant research expected to take another 3 to 6 months before a clearer view.
capex_capacity: 200 KLPD grain-based distillery: most equipment on site per management, with one or two items awaited; commissioning trials targeted for June 2026 (management earlier said Q1 FY27 and next month).
Adds approximately 60 million litres of annual ethanol capacity; management did not give capex, asset turns or EBITDA potential at normalised utilisation.
Maize-based ethanol to be bought under the government maize price for the blending programme; multi-feedstock benefits expected once the maize facility is running.
Bagasse supplies about 85% of energy and coal about 15%; energy costs described as stable.
Sathgen Therapeutics step-down subsidiary formed; CDSCO application for preliminary efficacy trial of the triple-negative breast cancer molecule planned for next quarter.
demand_pricing: Management reports higher import costs and narrower fossil-to-bio price gap, leading to an expected uptick in bio-based chemical demand in FY27. More than 20 bio-based molecules are made; some faced raw material and freight disruption from the West Asia crisis.
Ethanol prices are set by the government: management quoted net realisation of about INR60-plus/litre for B-heavy molasses, INR65-plus for juice and about INR72 for maize.
Ethanol supply is in surplus under the blending programme; industry has asked the government to revise ethanol prices, and management said a decision lies with the government.
Draft standards for E85, E100 and beyond E20 are cited as future demand drivers, but management gave no timeline for flex-fuel policy.
Management said the company is still weighing ethyl acetate margins against its long-term specialty chemicals goal, and that ethyl acetate was run when margins were better.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profitability fall from INR95 crore (31 March 2025) to INR66 crore (31 March 2026), and what will profitability look like next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin pressure to a higher sugarcane price for the last season without a matching increase in sugar MSP or ethanol prices. It pointed to better bio-based chemicals and maize ethanol contributions in the coming year, without a figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net realisation on ethanol by feedstock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said net realisation is about INR60-plus per litre from B-heavy molasses, INR65-plus from juice and about INR72 from maize; all prices are government-declared.

qa_highlights.question: Has the grain distillery equipment arrived and what margins are underwritten for maize ethanol?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all equipment is on site with one or two items pending, and commissioning trials are targeted for next month. Larger benefits are expected from the November ethanol year; management did not give a spread figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the specialty mix fall, and was the ethyl acetate ramp deliberate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was partly a margin call, since ethanol supply is in surplus and ethyl acetate margins were attractive, while the long-term aim is still more specialty chemicals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DME pilot status and what milestones are needed before commercialisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The lab work at ICT is complete and the pilot plant is running; management expects 3 to 6 more months of research before it can give a better answer.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a change in the ethanol price or policy outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Price revisions are for the government to decide. The industry has asked for higher blend pricing given sugarcane price rises over three years, and management pointed to E85/E100 draft standards as future demand support.

risks_watch: Ethanol prices are government-set, and the industry is seeking a revision; no timeline was given. Sugar MSP and ethanol prices were unchanged despite a higher cane price, which squeezed margins.
The 200 KLPD grain distillery is still in commissioning trials; utilisation, capex and maize spreads are not yet disclosed, so near-term contribution is uncertain.
West Asia-linked disruption affected raw material supply and freight for some bio-based chemicals in Q4; management said logistics hit the chemicals segment.
Specialty chemical share rose to 61%, but bio-based revenue was flat in FY26 (INR578 crore) and the revenue mix was largely unchanged from FY25.
Monsoon and cane pricing for next season remain open questions, and the DME and TNBC programmes are early-stage, with a 2 to 3 year timeline for out-licensing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the bio-based and ethanol outlook, but cautious and non-committal on pricing and policy. Management gave no numbers for the grain distillery's economics or for the TNBC and DME timelines, and deferred several questions to later periods or the government.
key_quotes: So, we are definitely seeing a stronger outlook in this financial year and this will be apparent from in the -- from this quarter onwards, that's the first point.
We achieved it as a nation by five years in advance.

The margin pressure took place because the government had announced a increased price of sugarcane for the last crushing season and did not increase the MSP of sugar and neither did they increase the price of the ethanol blend.

growth.why: Management guides to a stronger bio-based chemicals outlook from Q1 FY27 and a 200 KLPD (about 60 million litres/yr) grain distillery entering commissioning trials in June 2026, but gives no revenue growth percentage, and the call did not give capex or EBITDA for the new capacity.
